To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the impact of LUP on the SOC2 indicator is strongly dependent on the initial SOC stock, (2) the ALR indicator is strongly dependent of both the initial SOC stock and the LUP, (3) for the BPL indicator, the impact of LUC is strongly dependent on crop type and the impact of the LUP on SOC2 is strongly dependent on initial SOC stock and crop type.

the impact of agricultural LUP on soil organic carbon (C) and yield can be assessed by means of the indicators: soil organic C change (SOC2), biomass productivity loss (BLP) and additional land requirement (LR).
the impact of LUP on SOC2 and BPL is mainly determined by the initial SOC stock and soil type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework that may support the decision making process towards a sustainable agriculture.
developing a framework to evaluate the impact on SOC stock and yield of LUP under the AoP natural resource.
the development of a framework to evaluate the impact on soil quality of agricultural land use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LUP have an impact on SOC and yield, which is expressed as an increase in SOC2 and BPL, respectively, and an increase in ALR.
the LUP in the case study are not sustainable, as the ALR is higher than the area of protection.
the proposed indicators may assist in evaluating the effect of LUC on soil quality, but that further research is needed to improve their applicability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed LC(I)A framework may assist farmers in making informed decisions about their LUP, while also being useful for the AoP natural resource.
the developed framework may be used to evaluate the impact on SOC and yield of different LUP in relation to the area of protection of natural resources.

the proposed framework can be used as a decision support system to evaluate the impact on soil quality in terms SOC change and yield loss due to LUP, and the additional land requirement for compensating the yield loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developed framework can be used as a tool to evaluate the impact on SOC and yield in relation to the area of protection of natural resources.
the proposed indicators are able to distinguish between the impact of LUP on the soil and the corresponding change of yield.
the developed indicators may assist in identifying the most sustainable land use options.
